cases.question: What happens if a team uses an Aggregated Standard Traded Player Exception in a trade that would put Apron Team Salary over the Second Apron Level?

claims.text: The Transaction Restrictions Table assigns the Second Apron Level as the Applicable Apron Level for a team that acquires a player using an Aggregated Standard Traded Player Exception (row H).
claims.quote:
Team acquires a player using an Aggregated 
Standard Traded Player Exception (as described 
in Section 6(j)(1)(ii) below)

claims.text: Because the Applicable Apron Level for that transaction is the Second Apron Level, the trade is prohibited: a team may not engage in a Transaction Restrictions Table transaction if, immediately following it, the team's Apron Team Salary for that Salary Cap Year would exceed the Applicable Apron Level corresponding to that transaction.
claims.quote:
A Team may not engage in a transaction set forth in 
the Transaction Restrictions Table if, immediately 
following such transaction, the Team’s Apron Team 
Salary for such Salary Cap Year would exceed the 
“Applicable Apron Level ” that corresponds with 
such transaction in the table

claims.text: The CBA's own worked example applies this to the Aggregated Standard Traded Player Exception: Team D's proposed trade using that exception, which would leave a 2024-25 Apron Team Salary of $195 million, is prohibited because that exceeds the $189.5 million 2024-25 Second Apron Level.
claims.quote:
The proposed trade (a transaction set forth in 
row H of the Transaction Restrictions Table with an Applicable Apron 
Level of the Second Apron Level) is prohibited by Section  2(e)(2)(i)(A) 
above because, immediately following the trade, Team D’s 2024-25 Apron 
Team Salary would exceed $189.5  million (i.e., the 2024-25 Second 
Apron Level).

claims.text: In addition, a team that engages in such a transaction may not, for the remainder of that Salary Cap Year, have an Apron Team Salary exceeding the Applicable Apron Level (here, the Second Apron Level) corresponding to that transaction.
claims.quote:
A Team that engages in a transaction set forth in 
the Transaction Restrictions Table may not, for the 
remainder of such Salary Cap Year, have an Apron Team 
Salary that exceeds the Applicable Apron 
Level that corresponds with such transaction in the 
table.

claims.text: There is a transitional carve-out limited to the 2023-24 Salary Cap Year: notwithstanding Section 2(e)(2), a team that engages in one or more of the transactions in rows F through J (which includes row H, the Aggregated Standard Traded Player Exception) during 2023-24 will not, by virtue of engaging in that transaction, be prohibited from having a 2023-24 Apron Team Salary that exceeds the Applicable Apron Level for that year.
claims.quote:
a Team that engages in one or more of the transactions set 
forth in rows F through J in the Transaction Restrictions Table 
during the 2023-24 Salary Cap Year will not by virtue of engaging in 
any such transaction(s) be prohibited from having an Apron Team 
Salary in the 2023-24 Salary Cap Year that exceeds the Applicable 
Apron Level for such Salary Cap Year.

cases.question: When is a player still eligible for NBA Most Valuable Player if he did not play sixty-five Regular Season games?

claims.text: A player who did not play sixty-five Regular Season games is still eligible for NBA Most Valuable Player if he satisfies the second Award Eligibility Criterion: he (A) played in at least sixty-two (62) Regular Season games, (B) suffered a "season-ending injury," and (C) played in at least eighty-five percent (85%) of the Regular Season games played by his Team prior to suffering that injury.
claims.quote:
(2) the player (A) played in at least sixty-two (62) Regular Season games, 
(B) suffered a “season-ending injury” (as defined below), and (C) played in 
at least eighty-five percent (85%) of the Regular Season games played by his 
Team prior to the player suffering such injury.

claims.text: For this purpose, a "season-ending injury" is an injury that, in the opinion of a physician jointly selected by the NBA and Players Association, makes it substantially more likely than not that the player would be unable to play through the May 31 following the date of the injury.
claims.quote:
A “season-ending injury” is an injury that, in the 
opinion of a physician jointly selected by the NBA 
and Players Association, makes it substantially more 
likely than not that the player would be unable to 
play through the May 31 following the date of such 
injury

claims.text: In counting games for these criteria, a player is considered to have played in a Regular Season game if he played at least twenty (20) minutes of that game, except that for no more than two (2) Regular Season games per Season he is considered to have played in a game if he played at least fifteen (15) minutes and fewer than twenty (20) minutes.
claims.quote:
A player shall be considered to have played in a 
Regular Season game if he played at least twenty (20) 
minutes of such game, provided that in respect of no 
more than two (2) Regular Season games per Season, 
such player will be considered to have played in a 
Regular Season game if he played at least fifteen (15) 
minutes and fewer than twenty (20) minutes in such 
game.

claims.text: Separately, a player who fails to satisfy the Award Eligibility Criteria in a Season may nonetheless be deemed eligible for the Applicable Generally Recognized League Honors (which include NBA Most Valuable Player) if he prevails in either an Award Eligibility Grievance or an Extraordinary Circumstances Challenge for that Season; he may not bring both in the same Season.
claims.quote:
A player who fails to satisfy the Award Eligibility Criteria in 
a Season may nonetheless be deemed eligible for the 
Applicable Generally Recognized League Honors if he 
prevails in either an Award Eligibility Grievance or an 
Extraordinary Circumstances Challenge in respect of such 
Season in accordance with the procedures set forth in 
Sections 6(b) and 6(c) below.  A player may not bring both 
an Award Eligibility Grievance and an Extraordinary 
Circumstances Challenge in respect of the same Season.

claims.text: To prevail in an Award Eligibility Grievance, the player bears the burden of proving, by clear and convincing evidence, that the Team willfully limited his number of minutes played or games played during the Regular Season with the intention of depriving him of eligibility for one or more of the Applicable Generally Recognized League Honors for that Season; the sole remedy is that the player is deemed eligible.
claims.quote:
the player bears the burden of proving, by clear and 
convincing evidence, that the Team willfully limited the 
player’s number of minutes played or games played during 
the Regular Season with the intention of depriving the player 
of eligibility for one or more of the Applicable Generally 
Recognized League Honors for such Season.

claims.text: To prevail in an Extraordinary Circumstances Challenge, the player must prove that (A) due to extraordinary circumstances it was impracticable for him to play in one or more of the Regular Season games he missed, (B) he would have satisfied the sixty-five-game criterion had he played in every game he missed due to those extraordinary circumstances (assuming he would have played twenty minutes in each such missed game), and (C) as a result of the extraordinary circumstances, and taking into account the totality of the circumstances, it would be unjust to exclude him from eligibility.
claims.quote:
(A) Due to extraordinary circumstances, it was  
impracticable for him to play in one (1) or more of 
the Regular Season game(s) that he missed during 
such Season; 
(B) He wo uld have satisfied the Award Eligibility 
Criterion set forth in Section 6(a)(1) above if he had 
played in every game that he missed due to the 
extraordinary circumstances ( i.e., assuming that he 
would have played twenty (20) minutes in each such 
missed game); and  
(C) As a result of the extraordinary circumstances, and 
taking into account the totality of the circumstances, 
including whether the player did not play in other 
Regular Season games in which he could have played 
during such Season, it would be unjust to exclude the 
player from eligibility for the Applicable Generally 
Recognized League Honors for such Season.

cases.question: What counts toward the cap as Salary, and how is Team Salary determined?

claims.text: “Salary” is defined as a player’s Compensation for the Season covered by the Salary Cap Year, plus any other amount deemed to constitute Salary under the Agreement, but it excludes Unlikely Bonuses, benefits received under the Agreement (such as Article IV benefits, per diem, and moving expenses), and any portion of Compensation attributable to another Salary Cap Year; it also includes consideration received by a retired player that is deemed Salary under Article XIII.
claims.quote: “Salary” means, with respect to a Salary Cap Year, a player’s Compensation with respect to the Season covered by such Salary Cap Year, plus any other amount that is deemed to constitute Salary in accordance with the terms of this Agreement, not including Unlikely Bonuses, any benefits the player received in accordanc e with the terms of this Agreement (including, e.g., the benefits provided for by Article IV, per diem, and moving expenses), and any portion of the player’s Compensation that is attributable to another Salary Cap Year in accordance with this Agreement.

claims.text: “Team Salary” for a Salary Cap Year is the sum of all Salaries attributable to a Team’s active and former players, plus other amounts computed under Article VII, less applicable credit amounts computed under Article VII.
claims.quote: “Team Salary” means, with respect to a Salary Cap Year, the sum of all Salaries attributable to a Team’s active and former players pl us other amounts as computed in accordance with Article VII, less applicable credit amounts as computed in accordance with Article VII.

claims.text: Article VII, Section 4(a) governs the computation of Team Salary and states that all of the listed amounts shall be included, beginning with the aggregate Salaries of all active players (and former players to the extent the Agreement provides) attributable to a particular Salary Cap Year.
claims.quote: For purposes of computing Team Salary under this Agreement, all of the following amounts shall be included: (1) Subject to the rules set forth in this Article VII, the aggregate Salaries of all active players (and former players to the extent provided by the terms of this Agreement) attributable to a particular Salary Cap Year, including, without limitation:

claims.text: International player payments count as Salary: any amount above the Excluded International Player Payment Amounts paid by or at a Team’s direction to a non-NBA basketball team or other entity to induce a player playing professionally outside the United States to sign a Player Contract (or to secure that right) is deemed Salary in the form of a signing bonus.
claims.quote: Any amount in excess of the amounts set forth below (“Excluded International Player Payment Amount s”) paid or to be paid by or at the direction of any NBA Team to (i) any basketball team other than an NBA Team, or (ii) any other entity, organization, representative or person, for the purpose of inducing a player who is participating in the game of basketball as a professional outside of the United States to enter into a Player Contract or in connection with securing the right to enter into a Player Contract with such a player shall be deemed Salary (in the form of a signing bonus) to the player

claims.text: Performance Bonuses count toward Salary only if the bonus would be earned assuming the Team’s or player’s performance were identical to the performance in the immediately preceding Salary Cap Year (subject to the challenge procedures in Section 3(d)(2)-(4)).
claims.quote: any Performance Bonus (provided such Performance Bonus may be included in a Player Contract in accordance with Section 5(b) below), shall be included in Salary only if such Performance Bonus would be earned if the Team’s or player’s performance were identical to the performance in the immediately preceding Salary Cap Year.

claims.text: All Incentive Compensation described in Article II, Sections 3(b)(iii) and 3(c) is included in Salary.
claims.quote: All Incentive Compensation described in Article II, Sections 3(b)(iii) and 3(c) shall be included in Salary.

claims.text: For a one-year, 10-Day, or Rest-of-Season Contract at the Minimum Player Salary, the Salary counted is the lesser of the full Minimum Player Salary or the portion of it not reimbursed out of the League-wide benefits fund in Article IV, Section 6(h).
claims.quote: the Salary of every player who signs a one-year, 10-Day, or Rest-of-Season Contract for the Minimum Player Salary applicable to such player shall be the lesser of (1) such Minimum Player Salary, or (2) the portion of such Minimum Player Salary that is not reimbursed out of the League-wide benefits fund described in Article IV, Section 6(h).

cases.question: How much is the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception?

response.message: The cited passage needs inputs the question does not give: the Salary Cap Year (season) at issue, the Salary Cap for that Salary Cap Year, the Salary Cap for the 2023-24 Salary Cap Year. Add them and ask again.

claims.text: The Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception amount is set by a formula: it is $5 million for the 2023-24 Salary Cap Year, and for each subsequent Salary Cap Year it is $5 million multiplied by a fraction whose numerator is the Salary Cap for that Salary Cap Year and whose denominator is the Salary Cap for the 2023-24 Salary Cap Year. Because the question names no Salary Cap Year and supplies neither Salary Cap figure, the dollar amount cannot be computed.
claims.quote: For the 2023-24 Salary Cap Year: $5 million For each subsequent Salary Cap Year: $5 million multiplied by a fraction, the numerator of which is the Salary Cap for that Salary Cap Year and the denominator of which is the Salary Cap for the 2023-24 Salary Cap Year

cases.question: An Early Qualifying Veteran Free Agent has a prior regular salary of 10000000 and the prior average player salary is 12000000. What is the first-year cap under the veteran free agent exception?

claims.text: For an Early Qualifying Veteran Free Agent, the first-year Salary plus Unlikely Bonuses may be up to the greater of (A) 175% of the Regular Salary for the final Salary Cap Year of the prior Contract or (B) 105% of the Average Player Salary for the prior Salary Cap Year. Applying the given inputs: (A) 175% × $10,000,000 = $17,500,000; (B) 105% × $12,000,000 = $12,600,000. The greater amount is $17,500,000, so the first-year cap under the Veteran Free Agent Exception is $17,500,000.
claims.quote:

final Salary Cap Year covered by his prior Contract, plus one 
hundred seventy-five percent (175%) of any Likely Bonuses 
and Unlikely Bonuses, respectively, called for in the final 
Salary Cap Year covered by the player’s prior Contract, or 
(B) Salary plus Unlikely Bonuses totaling an amount equal to

cases.question: How many seasons can a contract signed with the mid-level exception run for a team that is over the Salary Cap?

response.message: More than one retrieved passage applies, and none says which one controls. Which season or effective date do you mean?

claims.text: Under the Non-Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception — the mid-level exception available to a team whose Team Salary is at or above the Salary Cap — a signed contract may run no more than four (4) Seasons.
claims.quote:
The term of a Player Contract signed pursuant to the 
Non-Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception may not exceed four (4) 
Seasons in length

claims.text: Under the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception — also a mid-level exception, used where the team's Apron Team Salary immediately following use exceeds the First Apron Level — a signed contract may run no more than two (2) Seasons.
claims.quote:
A Team may use the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception to 
sign one (1) or more Player Contracts during each Salary Cap Year 
not to exceed two (2) Seasons in length

cases.question: What can't a second-apron team do in a trade?

claims.text: A Second Apron Team is prohibited from trading (conditionally or unconditionally) its first round draft pick in the first NBA Draft that occurs following the seventh Season that follows the Season occurring within that Salary Cap Year.
claims.quote: (i) the Team shall be prohibited from trading (either conditionally or unconditionally) its first round draft pick in the first NBA Draft that occurs following the seventh Season that follows the Season occurring within such Salary Cap Year; and

claims.text: The CBA's own illustration: a team that is a Second Apron Team for the 2024-25 Salary Cap Year would be prohibited from trading its 2032 first round draft pick.
claims.quote: Example:  If Team A is a Second Apron Team for the 2024-25 Salary Cap Year, then it would be prohibited from trading its 2032 first round draft pick (i.e., its first round draft pick in the first NBA Draft that occurs following the seventh Season that follows the Season occurring within such Salary Cap Year).
